La documentación de esta integración la escribe su autor y, por ahora, solo está disponible en inglés.

:::

Brings your iAquaLink pool systems into Gladys, through the iAquaLink cloud
(the one of the iAquaLink mobile app):

- **Jandy iAquaLink panels** (iQ20, AquaLink RS with an iAquaLink module):
  pool, spa and air temperatures, pool and spa pumps, pool, spa and solar
  heaters, pool and spa set points, lights (on/off, brightness of dimmable
  lights), auxiliary outputs, and pH, ORP and salinity when the panel reports
  them;
- **Zodiac eXO iQ chlorinators**: water temperature, pH, ORP, their set
  points, chlorine production level, chlorine production on/off, boost, low
  mode, filter pump, auxiliary outputs, heating (on/off and set point) when a
  heating module is present, and a status text (error code, low salt).

> This integration has **never been tested on a real iAquaLink account or
> system yet**: it is a port of the
> [iaqualink-py](https://github.com/flz/iaqualink-py) library used by Home
> Assistant, checked against sample answers only. Feedback is welcome on the
> [Gladys forum](https://community.gladysassistant.com/t/10385).
>
> Unofficial: not affiliated with Zodiac, Jandy or Fluidra.

## Set up

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**, install **Zodiac / Jandy iAquaLink**.
2. In its configuration, enter the **email** and **password** of your
   iAquaLink account (the ones you use in the iAquaLink app). The password is
   a secret field: Gladys never shows it again, and the integration sends it
   only to the iAquaLink sign-in service.
3. The status shows **Connected to iAquaLink** and the number of pool systems.
   Open the **Discovery** tab and add your systems.

The **Test the connection** button signs in and reads the account at once (at
most every 30 seconds), and gives a short summary.

## Options

| Option                           | Default | What it does                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Allow commands from Gladys       | off     | The pool is only read until you tick it. Then: pumps, heaters, set points, lights and the eXO switches.             |
| Also allow the auxiliary outputs | off     | The plain auxiliaries and valve actuators of the panel, and the aux outputs of the eXO. Needs the option above too. |
| Show the unnamed auxiliaries     | off     | Auxiliaries still named "Aux 3", "Aux V12" or "Extra Aux" on the panel are left out unless this box is ticked.      |
| Refresh interval (seconds)       | 60      | How often the pool is read: 30 seconds at the fastest.                                                              |
| Language                         | French  | Names of the features of the systems added from now on, and the status text.                                        |

An auxiliary output can drive anything wired to it: a cleaner, a water
feature, but also a **valve** (spa spillover, solar...), and the iAquaLink
valve actuators (SJVA) are auxiliaries too. That is why they have their own
option, off by default: tick it only if commanding them from Gladys is safe
for your installation.

## Limits of use

- iAquaLink publishes no API nor quota: the integration uses the endpoints
  of the iAquaLink app, like Home Assistant. It reads every system at the
  refresh interval (two requests for a panel, one for an eXO), the list of
  systems every 30 minutes, and never sends more than 20 requests a minute,
  commands included.
- After an error it waits 1, 2, 5, 10 then 15 minutes; when iAquaLink asks to
  slow down (HTTP 429) it pauses for the time asked (15 minutes otherwise),
  commands included.
- A refused email or password is not tried again for 6 hours, or at once
  after you change it (or with the Test button), so the account is not locked.
- The session (IdToken) is renewed before it expires; a refused refresh token
  leads to one new sign-in, never more than one every 5 minutes. A sign-in
  without any answer (internet box still starting after a power cut...)
  follows the normal pauses of 1 to 15 minutes. After three sign-ins in a row
  that the service answers badly (5xx error, unreadable answer), the next try
  waits 1 hour, or a change of the email or the password, or the "Test the
  connection" button.

## How commands work

The pumps, heaters and plain auxiliaries of an iAquaLink panel only know a
**toggle** command. So, for each command, the integration:

1. reads the state of the panel again, right before (within 4 seconds:
   Gladys waits 5 seconds for the answer; a slower read sends nothing);
2. refuses when the panel is offline, or when the state of the equipment
   cannot be read;
3. sends nothing when the equipment is already in the asked state;
4. otherwise toggles once. For the next 60 seconds, unless the panel already
   reports the change, the equipment is expected in its new state: asking it
   again succeeds without sending anything, asking the old state is refused
   (a second toggle would undo the first one).

Commands of one system run one at a time. Dimmable and colour lights, set
points and every eXO command take an absolute value instead. Set points must
stay between 1 and 40 °C (34 and 104 °F); a panel paired with a heat pump
receives them through the heat pump command, like in the iAquaLink app.

A colour light turned on starts on its first colour (the effects are not
handled yet).

## Not supported yet

- Robot cleaners (i2d, Vortex, Cyclobat), standalone Zodiac heat pumps and
  iQPump: they are counted as "not supported yet" in the status.
- OneTouch scenes, the variable-speed pumps of a panel, IntelliCenter light
  zones, colour effects, the controls of a heat pump paired with a panel.

## Privacy

The email and password stay in the Gladys configuration. The integration
keeps only, in its `/data` volume, the features and auxiliaries already seen
and the temperature unit of each system, so the Discovery tab stays the same
after a restart. No token or password is ever written to disk or to the logs.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que Zodiac / Jandy iAquaLink te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your iAquaLink pool | `section` | No | Brings your iAquaLink pool systems into Gladys through the iAquaLink cloud: Jandy iAquaLink panels (pool, spa and air temperatures, pumps, heaters and set points, lights, auxiliaries) and Zodiac eXO iQ chlorinators (chlorine production, boost, pH, ORP, water temperature, status). Enter the email and password of your iAquaLink app account, then add your systems from the Discovery tab. Commands stay off until you allow them below. The cloud is read every minute by default (30 seconds at the fastest), with longer pauses after errors. Unofficial, not affiliated with Zodiac, Jandy or Fluidra; never tested on a real system yet. |
| iAquaLink email | `string` | Sí | The email you sign in to the iAquaLink app with. |
| iAquaLink password | `secret` | Sí | Kept by Gladys, sent only to the iAquaLink sign-in service, never shown again nor logged. |
| Allow commands from Gladys | `boolean` | No | Off by default: the pool is only read. Once ticked: pumps, heaters, set points, lights and the switches of the eXO chlorinator. Each command reads the state again just before it is sent. |
| Also allow the auxiliary outputs | `boolean` | No | The plain auxiliaries of the panel, its valve actuators and the aux outputs of the eXO can drive anything, a valve included: they stay read-only unless this box (and the one above) is ticked. |
| Show the unnamed auxiliaries | `boolean` | No | Auxiliaries still named "Aux 3", "Aux V12" or "Extra Aux" on the panel are usually unused: they are left out unless this box is ticked. |
| Refresh interval (seconds) | `number` | No | How often the pool is read: 30 seconds at the fastest, to stay gentle with the iAquaLink cloud. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Used for the names of the features of the systems added from now on, and for the status text. |

## Cómo instalar Zodiac / Jandy iAquaLink en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: Zodiac / Jandy iAquaLink aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-iaqualink:0.1.2`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-iaqualink](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-iaqualink).

Zodiac / Jandy iAquaLink requiere Gladys `>=5.1.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.
